examples.en: The child laughs happily riding the wooden horse.
There is an old wooden horse at the playground.
Do you know the story of the Trojan horse?
My younger sibling rocked back and forth on the rocking horse.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 손자에게 나무 목마를 만들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandpa made a wooden toy horse for his grandson.
This rocking horse has been here since I was a baby.

explain: 목마는 말 모양 장난감이나 놀이기구 말에 써요. 아이를 어깨에 태우는 '목말'과 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리지만 서로 다른 말이에요. '트로이 목마'는 컴퓨터 바이러스 이야기에도 나와요.
explain_en: 목마 refers to a toy horse or a ride horse. It sounds close to 목말 (carrying a child on the shoulders), but they are different words. 트로이 목마 also appears in talk about computer viruses.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 후반에 두 골을 실점했어요.
examples.en: Our team conceded two goals in the second half.
The defense wobbled and we ended up conceding.
Everyone fell back so as not to concede.
Every time we conceded, the coach called a timeout.
If you concede first, it is hard to turn the game around.
The pitcher who gave up runs in a row was replaced.

explain: '득점하다'와 짝을 이루는 스포츠 말이에요. 축구나 야구 중계에서 '실점 없이 막았다'처럼 자주 들려요. 일상에서는 '점수를 내주다'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: This is the sports pair of '득점하다' (to score). You often hear it in soccer and baseball broadcasts, as in '실점 없이 막았다'. In casual talk people also say '점수를 내주다'.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 마지막에 극적인 역전승을 거뒀어요.
examples.en: Our team scored a dramatic comeback win at the end.
Yesterday's game was a comeback win, so it was even more fun.

examples.ko: 두 골 뒤지다가 역전승을 하다니 믿기지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't believe they won from two goals behind.
Everyone was happy to hear the comeback news.
The coach said the secret to the comeback was stamina.
In baseball, comeback wins excite fans the most.

explain: 역전승은 지고 있다가 뒤집어서 이긴 경기예요. 반대는 '역전패'이고, 처음부터 크게 이기는 것은 '압승'이에요. 보통 '역전승을 거두다'나 '역전승을 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 역전승 is a win after trailing. Its opposite is 역전패, and winning big from the start is 압승. It usually appears as 역전승을 거두다 or 역전승을 하다.

examples.en: The mermaid in the fairy tale lives in the sea.
Do you know the story of the little mermaid?
The child sleeps holding a mermaid doll.
I want to swim as well as a mermaid.
A mermaid statue stands at the beach.
I watched a movie where a mermaid becomes a human.

explain: 대부분 동화 '인어공주'로 접하는 말이에요. 수영을 아주 잘하는 사람을 '인어 같다'고 비유하기도 해요. 가장 흔한 짝말은 '인어공주', '인어 동상'이에요.
explain_en: Most people meet this word through the fairy tale '인어공주' (The Little Mermaid). Someone who swims very well can be called '인어 같다'. Common pairings are '인어공주' and '인어 동상'.

examples.ko: 저는 인터넷으로 해외 직구를 자주 해요.
examples.en: I often buy things directly from overseas online.
The clothes I bought directly from abroad arrived in a week.

examples.ko: 직구는 배송비와 세금을 꼭 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: With overseas purchases you must check the shipping fee and taxes.
That pitcher's fastball is very quick.

examples.ko: 감독은 변화구 대신 직구로 승부하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The manager said to go with the fastball instead of breaking balls.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 말을 돌리지 않고 직구로 말해요.
examples.en: That friend speaks straight, without beating around the bush.

explain: 쇼핑 이야기에서는 해외 사이트에서 직접 사는 것이고, 야구에서는 휘지 않고 곧게 오는 빠른 공이에요. 야구에서 반대는 '변화구'예요. 쇼핑은 '직구하다'로도 말해요. 대화에서 '직구로 말하다'처럼 비유로도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 항상 직구로 말해서 편해요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구의 직구처럼 변화구 없이 곧바로 말한다는 뜻이에요. 돌려 말하지 않아서 솔직하다는 칭찬으로도, 너무 직접적이라는 뜻으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like a fastball with no breaking pitch, you say it straight. It can be praise for being honest or a hint that someone is too direct.

explain_en: In shopping talk, 직구 means buying directly from overseas sites, and in baseball it is the fast ball that flies straight. In baseball its opposite is 변화구 (breaking ball). For shopping you can also say 직구하다. It is also used figuratively, as in 직구로 말하다.

examples.en: A friend sang a congratulatory song at the wedding.
Who is going to sing the celebration song?

examples.ko: 축가 연습을 매일 저녁에 하고 있어요.
examples.en: I practice the celebration song every evening.
Which song should we choose for the celebration?
The song lifted the whole mood.
The song at my sibling's wedding was so moving.

explain: 결혼식에서 가장 많이 들어요. 보통 친구나 가수가 신랑 신부를 위해 부르고 '축가를 부르다'로 같이 써요. 생일에 부르는 노래는 '축가'보다 '생일 노래'라고 해요.
explain_en: You hear it mostly at weddings, where a friend or singer performs for the couple. It pairs with 부르다: '축가를 부르다'. For a birthday, people say 생일 노래 rather than 축가.
